question: What are the rewards of memorizing the Qur'an, and what practical advice helps in memorizing it?
asked: A sister writes that she watched the entire Qur'an series, the summary of the Qur'an, and she is now inspired to memorize the whole Qur'an. Are there any specific rewards, and what advice would you give her?
answer:
So to answer that question: first and foremost, of course, there are many rewards. And I thank Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala that you have been inspired to memorize the Qur'an after the month of Ramadan. In fact, inshaAllah, this is a good sign that your deeds have been accepted, because one of the signs of the acceptance of a deed is the intention to do more deeds after the acceptance of the first deed. And so alhamdulillah, this is a very positive sign.

And may I encourage all of the viewers, without exception, to intend to memorize bits and pieces of the Qur'an, even if it's just the last 10 surahs, or if it's just Tabarak, or if it's just Surah Kahf, or if it's just Surah Yasin, or if it's just Surah Rahman. Just start memorizing, and then bit by bit continue to do that.

As for the rewards, I can give you many, many lectures, and there are many lectures online. I'll just quote you two or three hadith. Of them is that the Prophet ﷺ said, inna lillahi ahlina min al-nas: that Allah has people that are chosen of mankind. And so they said, who are Allah's chosen of mankind? So the Prophet ﷺ said, ahl al-Qur'an, the people of the Qur'an; hum ahlu Allahi wa khassatuhu: they are like the chosen, or the family, of Allah, and they are the ones whom Allah ʿazza wa jall has preferred. So the Prophet said the Ahl al-Qur'an are the ones whom Allah has chosen.

And in another hadith in Abu Dawood, our Prophet said that of the ways to show respect to Allah is to honor three people:

- Number one, to honor the Muslim who has white hair, meaning that he is elderly. So to show honor to our elderly, a righteous man or a righteous woman who is elderly and has whitish hair: you show honor and respect to him.
- Number two, the one who is a carrier of the Qur'an, the hafidh of the Qur'an, the one who does not go to extremes either way, the one who is the moderate carrier of the Qur'an. So the one who acts upon the Qur'an and who embodies the Qur'an: we show respect to the hafidh of the Qur'an.
- And number three, the ruler that is a righteous ruler: we show respect to the righteous ruler, because it is a great responsibility that he or she has fulfilled.

And another hadith in this regard is the one where the Prophet ﷺ said that it will be said to the companion of the Qur'an (the companion of the Qur'an means, obviously, the one who is associating himself with it, constantly reciting it, and when you memorize the Qur'an, you must constantly recite it), it will be said to the companion of the Qur'an on the Day of Judgment: recite, and rise up as you are reciting. And so as he is reciting, he will continue to rise up, and the last verse that he recites will decide his place in Jannah. And based upon this, some of our scholars said that the highest place of Jannah is for those who have memorized the Qur'an and understood it and act upon it (may Allah ʿazza wa jall make us amongst them), because for every verse that they recite, they will rise one degree in Jannah. And so how can there not be blessings? And there are many, many more blessings than this.

Now, a brief summary of the practical tips. I have an article online (you can just Google it, "Tips for Memorizing the Qur'an" by Yasir Qadhi), but I can just summarize that article for you. Realize that memorizing the Qur'an is a spiritual and a physical project. It is a combination of that which is a supernatural blessing along with a natural mechanism. Therefore, it is a miracle and a blessing that you can strive for. It's together; it's dual. And if you want to take advantage of this blessing, then you should be in a position to receive it, and strive for it both spiritually and physically, to get the maximum benefit. So I have quick pointers that you should follow.

First and foremost, sincerity. You are memorizing the Qur'an first and foremost for the pleasure of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, not to show off and not to tell other people. Sincerity is a factor, and you need to be sincere.

Number two, the rules of tajweed. Tajweed really helps you to memorize, and tajweed means the science of reciting the Qur'an. It is one of the easiest sciences in all of Islam, and it is just simple rules: where do you elongate? Where do you do the ghunnah? How do you pronounce the R? So find a tajweed teacher; online as well, there are plenty of teachers. Find a tajweed teacher of your own gender if you can, and just recite with them one-on-one and memorize the rules of tajweed, and you will yourself begin to enjoy the recitation better.

Number three, consistency. Consistency is very important. It is essential to be consistent when you memorize. There should be no vacation. Memorization should occur seven days a week. There is no "five days, and then after, if you're able to." Obviously, if you're not able to, do whatever you can, but the more consistent you are, the better it is. There are no vacations when it comes to the worship of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, and therefore there should be no vacation when it comes to memorization.

Memorization is very much like going to the gym for your body. When you go every single day and you're lifting whatever weights you're lifting, in the beginning it's really difficult, but Allah created the memory like the muscles: the more you exercise, the easier it is. And once you go daily to the gym, what was very difficult in the beginning becomes very easy within a week or two. And if you don't go to the gym for a few weeks, a few months, what happens? Well, the memory is more in need of the gym than your body is. And so go to the spiritual gym and go to the memorization gym every single day, and make sure that you memorize, even if it is just two lines, three lines, but be consistent. You must memorize as regularly as possible. And my advice is: do not skip even one day. Memorize every single day, even if it is one or two lines.

The next thing is timing. When should you memorize? You should memorize early in the morning. The best time to memorize is right after the Fajr prayer, or even before Fajr, but after Fajr is typically the best, even before you have breakfast. After you pray Fajr, when it is all quiet and nothing else is going on, open up the Qur'an and begin to memorize.

And by the way, I remember when I was a teenager, I would begin by memorizing a page a day. And when I started memorizing the first page, it would take me an hour, an hour and 20 minutes to memorize. And by the time five, six months had gone, I was memorizing a page in 15, 20 minutes, literally. It went down to one fourth of the original time. And I remember this clearly myself: "Oh, okay, I memorized it, good, move on." So that's what is going to happen if you do it every single time. And obviously I'm speaking of when I was a teenager. I understand when we're older; I cannot memorize a page of something new now, that's not going to be possible. But the point is, you try, and it will become better, inshaAllah.

Also, atmosphere. Have a secluded place, have a consistent place, have a specific chair or a specific area of the house where there's nothing else going on. Make sure your cell phone is turned off and upside down. Don't scroll through the news. Don't hear the beeps when they're coming; that's not going to help you. You need to have a calm atmosphere without any distractions. Make sure everybody knows not to disturb you in that regular routine. As I said, you must have the regular timing, regular atmosphere, regular consistency. Make it into a habit.

And in fact, I even say you should have complete familiarity: start at the same time, and start in the same physical location, and use the same mushaf every single day. You need to have your special copy of the mushaf, of the Qur'an, and that will be your most prized copy. It's going to be your go-to copy for memorization, because memorization is also visual: you will see, and it will become in your memory. Even to this day, generally speaking, if you quote me a verse, I can close my eyes and I can visualize where it is on the page of the Qur'an I memorized: is it on the right-hand page, left-hand page, up or down? Roughly, generally, it's still there, because that's what happens when you memorize with one particular mushaf.

And as for how you memorize, there is no magic trick. There is no easy way. You repeat, you repeat, you repeat, you repeat, and then you repeat again. It's just repetition. There's no magic trick to do it. You just literally have to repeat that verse, and then repeat it, and then repeat it, and then close your eyes and repeat it, and keep on doing it over and over again. And it always helps to listen to somebody, even if it's on audio or whatnot, to listen to a recitation online before you begin to memorize.

Also, of the tips that I can give you is to memorize with meaning: understand what you are memorizing. Read the translation of what you're going to memorize and understand the words, so that you have an idea. Read the tafsirs, listen to the tafsirs.

Another point is: surround yourself with recitation. Don't just let those 10 or 15 minutes be what you're memorizing of the day. If you're going to memorize at 6:30 a.m., let's say seven o'clock comes and that's it, you close the Qur'an. When you're going to work, turn the Qur'an on. When you're doing something in the household that doesn't require you to talk (so for example, if you're doing the dishes or you're cleaning or whatnot), it is allowed to listen to the Qur'an in the background as long as you have some attention. What is not allowed is you put the Qur'an on and then you're rude to the recitation by talking to other people; no. But if you put the Qur'an in the background and you are listening to it, even as you do your chores, that is absolutely fine, because you are listening at some level. And the purpose of that listening is to reinforce your memory. So surround yourself with Qur'anic recitation.

Also, if possible, another point (I've forgotten the numbers here, I'm just saying them): find a recitation buddy. Get a friend who wants to memorize, so that you can keep each other in check, and call each other every day and recite to each other. And then it'll also be like a competition. It'll be a human incentive, which is halal here: your niyyah is for Allah, but you're using somebody to just give you positive peer pressure. So you know you have to recite to somebody at seven o'clock, let's say, and he's going to recite to you, and so you have that positive peer pressure. Find a recitation buddy. Just like when you go to the gym, you have somebody to spot you, to help out, because it just psychologically gets you in the mood.

Also, another pointer is that whatever you've memorized, recite it in that day's salah, and then continue to recite it. Stop reciting just Inna a'taynaka al-kawthar and Surat al-Ikhlas; move on to the surah that you're memorizing. If you're memorizing Surah Tabarak, start reciting Surah Tabarak in all of your salawat, and make sure that it is a constant thing that you do, so that you have some memory of the recitation.

Also, the issue of what you should be doing. So suppose you have half an hour, let's say from 6:30 to 7 o'clock, that you've dedicated to the memorization of the Qur'an. You need to divide your time with the Qur'an into three parts. The bulk of it, maybe I would say at least 50 to 60% of it, is going to be the new memorization. How much you memorize depends on your time frame. When I was memorizing full time, I did a page a day, but obviously that's very difficult for many people. Start with two lines, two lines a day, so that inshaAllah within a week you'll finish a page. It's a big deal: "Oh mashaAllah, in two weeks you're going to be done." Like, oh mashaAllah. So do something. So you're going to spend maybe 50% of that time frame memorizing that new section.

The next 20%, you're going to go over the recitation and the memorization of the previous seven days. So the seven days before the one that you memorized: you will go over that and connect it. And then you will recite to somebody the previous seven days' memorization along with today's memorization, because again, you memorize in snippets. How will you connect those snippets? Imagine a chain, another chain, another chain. Every day you're having a chain, chain, chain, chain. What's going to happen? Those chains are going to be disconnected. You have to memorize the linkage as well. The way you're going to do that: you will go over the last seven days' recitation along with today's recitation, and that's going to be an eight-day solid amount. So if you memorize two lines a day, then the last seven days will be 14 lines, and then today's will be another two, so you'll recite 16 lines in that day. If it's two lines a day; if it's three lines, it'll be more than that.

Because the easiest section of the Qur'an to forget is what you just memorized last week, what you just freshly memorized. It's like you just gently drew something in the sand. That's how the first memorization is. If you don't do anything, the wind will come and it will erase it. You have to keep on drawing, drawing, drawing, until you hit, metaphorically, the rock, and then you can carve it into the rock. That's what you need to keep on doing.

So imagine a caterpillar; this is the way I put it to my students. The head of the caterpillar is today's memorization. So every day you take one step forward. The body of the caterpillar is seven segments. Every day you take it one little bit more, more, more. So then you're going to have that one caterpillar. So that's going to be two things: number one is the daily memorization; number two is the last seven days.

There's one thing left: how about the rest of the Qur'an that the caterpillar has left behind, metaphorically? That will be your next section: at least every single day, you need to do some level of a page or two of some of the previous stuff. So imagine the caterpillar going: it leaves behind, mashaAllah, tabarakAllah, an amount. So as it keeps on going, that amount will have another caterpillar, and that's going to be faster. You'll be doing maybe four pages, three pages.

And you don't have to do this at the same time. Ideally, the memorization and the previous seven pages will be, let's say, in the morning. Then you come at Asr time, Maghrib time; now you have a little bit of a different memory thing, and now you can go to the previous old memory, not the fresh memory. So suppose that you're memorizing Juz Tabarak, let's say. So that will be: okay, I memorized Juz 'Amma two months ago; now I'm going to be doing two pages of Juz 'Amma, three pages of Juz 'Amma. So you do something from your old memory, and that's going to be constant. Eventually, you're going to reach your goal. Your goal is, let's say, to memorize Surah Yasin to Surah al-Nas. When you finish that goal, then you will increase your daily recitation of your old memory. But you can never, ever just stop, because you must constantly keep on doing it, and that is how you will become the sahib, or the companion, of the Qur'an.

And the last point that I'm going to say (all of this is advice that I myself have done, and people have taught me when I was doing it), the last point I'll say is: do not jump around the Qur'an. It is, in my estimation, a mistake. Be consistent; start from one place and work your way. Now, you can do large chunks. So for example, if you've done, let's say, Juz Tabarak to Surah al-Nas and you have two juz down, then your goal is, "I want to do Yasin and Kahf and Rahman and Baqarah," let's say. Okay, understandable, you're going to pick and choose. But if you intend to memorize the whole Qur'an, or even like 15 juz solid, do not just pick and choose a surah at random. There should be some consistency. So you build big blocks; you don't build small blocks. You go continuously. And if you want to switch, it should be after you've done a good amount from one side; then you go to another side, and then you can connect the dots. But whatever you do, don't just have one thing here, one thing here, one thing here.

And then the last point, and definitely not the least, but definitely very important: you raise your hands up to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala and you make du'a to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala that Allah makes the memorization of the Qur'an easy for you. May Allah facilitate this for you.
